definitions.gloss: proposer; advocate; originator of an idea
definitions.explanation: The person who first put forward a theory, method, or movement and argues for it publicly. Used mainly of academic, technical, and social ideas rather than of everyday suggestions.

examples.japanese: この{理論|りろん}の{提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}だ。
examples.english: He is the originator of this theory.

examples.japanese: {提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}{本人|ほんにん}が{講演|こうえん}に{来|き}た。
examples.english: The originator himself came to give the lecture.

examples.japanese: その{運動|うんどう}の{提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}は、{当時|とうじ}まだ{無名|むめい}の{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}だった。
examples.english: The person who first advocated that movement was, at the time, still an unknown researcher.

notes:
Formed from {提唱|ていしょう} (advocacy, proposing) plus 〜{者|しゃ} (person who). Usually appears after の naming what was proposed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {理論|りろん}の{提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}: the originator of a theory
- {提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}として{知|し}られる: to be known as the person who proposed it
- {最初|さいしょ}の{提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}: the first to advocate it
- {提唱者|ていしょうしゃ}の{一人|ひとり}: one of the proponents

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {創始者|そうししゃ}: founder — stresses starting an organization or school, not arguing for an idea
- {推進者|すいしんしゃ}: promoter — pushes an idea forward without necessarily having originated it
